run: sh -c 'for c in pwsh pwsh.exe "/c/Program Files/PowerShell/7/pwsh" "/c/Program Files/PowerShell/7/pwsh.exe" "/mnt/c/Program Files/PowerShell/7/pwsh.exe" "/mnt/c/Program Files/PowerShell/7/pwsh"; do if command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x "$c" ]; then exec "$c" -NoProfile -File ./scripts/check-powershell.ps1; fi; done; echo "TOOL MISSING: pwsh (PowerShell 7) is on no PATH and at no known Windows location, so the .ps1 checks DID NOT RUN. This is a missing tool, not a failed check. Install PowerShell 7." >&2; exit 127'
rules.why: 3s. Every .ps1 here is Windows-only end to end, so a call to a cmdlet that does not exist parses cleanly and fails only on the one platform nothing here can run. PROVEN red by appending Invoke-TotallyMadeUpCmdlet to plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/guard.ps1. The interpreter is RESOLVED, not named. This file is TRACKED as of 2026-09-14, so it travels to clones that are not this machine, and a hardcoded /c/Program Files/PowerShell/7/pwsh fails on every one of them - verify-gate.sh runs this command and blocks completion on a non-zero exit, so even a Linux clone with pwsh ON PATH was blocked by this rule. Order matters: bare `pwsh` first, then `pwsh.exe` and the Windows locations with AND without the .exe suffix - under WSL the reachable binary is the Windows one and is named pwsh.exe, so omitting the suffix reported TOOL MISSING on a box where PowerShell was installed and usable, because CLAUDE.md records that a bare `pwsh` is not always on Git Bash's PATH. When nothing resolves it exits 127 with TOOL MISSING on stderr rather than 0 - a tool that could not run must never report as a check that passed. NOTE the script's two known limitations (README of _verify): CI mode enumerates via `git ls-files`, so an UNTRACKED .ps1 is invisible to it, and `param([string]$Path)` takes one path, silently dropping the rest of a list.
